question: Can a pipeline given only sampled areas under generated curves recover symbolic antiderivatives and then induce human-readable integration rules without direct calculus demonstrations?

key_findings.claim: The pipeline converts numerical quadrature into symbolic pseudo-labels, distills those labels into a sequence model, and separately searches a restricted coefficient grammar for rules.
key_findings.evidence: For each generated function, 10,000 trapezoidal samples on x in [0,4] define the definite integral. A pretrained symbolic regressor proposes an expression and cases above 1% relative error are discarded. GPT-Neo or Flan-T5 maps the original expression to that proposal, while a coefficient search tries linear relations and arithmetic combinations with absolute R-squared above 0.95.

key_findings.claim: On held-out samples drawn from the same narrow generators, GPT-Neo reproduces the symbolic-regression teacher more accurately and faster than directly rerunning that teacher.
key_findings.evidence: For 10,000 polynomial and 10,000 exponential/sine/cosine test functions, GPT-Neo reports exact accuracy 73.3% and 87.1%, approximate accuracy 95.7% and 94.8%, and 0.722-second latency. Flan-T5 scores 67.7%/64.6% exact, while the symbolic regressor scores 65.7%/46.4% exact at 3.17 seconds.

key_findings.claim: The rule search recovers the expected power, exponential, sine, and cosine antiderivative templates inside the hand-specified function families.
key_findings.evidence: Coefficient regressions recover a'_k=a_(k-1)/k for degree-at-most-six polynomials; division of amplitude by frequency recovers the exponential and trigonometric coefficients and the x=0 integration constant. Reported coefficient correlations are essentially one for these templates.

anchors.section: 4.4.2 Rules of Integral for exp Function
4.4.3 Rules of Integral for sin Function

key_findings.claim: Calling the result discovery from only the definition of integration overstates how much prior structure the system receives.
key_findings.evidence: The polynomial source is AMPS parametric algebra; function templates and operators are chosen by the author; the symbolic regressor has been trained to map curves to expressions; GPT-Neo is pretrained on 1.99 million AMPS algebra/number-theory pairs; and rule search is explicitly restricted to named coefficients, arithmetic operators, and a chosen R-squared threshold. These priors contain much of the representation and hypothesis class needed to expose the rules.

key_findings.claim: The evaluation measures interpolation within templates, not discovery of an unseen mathematical law.
key_findings.evidence: Training and test functions use the same polynomial and a*sin(bx)+c, a*cos(bx)+c, a*exp(bx)+c generators; there is no template-held-out split, composition-depth shift, singular case, unknown operator, independent theorem checker, or comparison on an open problem. Approximate correctness is measured against rounded pseudo-label expressions rather than derivative equivalence to the input.

key_findings.claim: The stated Flan-T5 model identity is internally inconsistent, preventing exact reproduction from the paper alone.
key_findings.evidence: The text calls the model Flan-T5-large with 783M parameters, but its footnote links to google/flan-t5-base. The paper also gives only aggregate curves and selected hyperparameters, without seeds, confidence intervals, decoding settings, source code, or the complete filtered split.

method.core_idea: Use numerical area as a weak oracle, recover candidate formulas with symbolic regression, then distill and compress recurring coefficient relations into explicit rules.
method.mechanism: Generate restricted analytic functions; sample cumulative trapezoidal areas; infer and filter symbolic expressions; round constants to two decimals; train autoregressive or encoder-decoder Transformers on expression pairs; group outputs by a chosen expression skeleton and exhaustively test simple coefficient transforms until a high-correlation rule appears.
assumptions: Numerical quadrature on one finite interval distinguishes the relevant symbolic expressions.
The symbolic-regression teacher's accepted outputs are structurally and numerically correct.
Two-decimal tokenization preserves the intended law.
The true rule lies in the manually supplied operator grammar and function skeleton.
Random train/test instances from identical templates are evidence of discovery rather than template interpolation.

techniques.role: Cumulative trapezoidal integration supplies values without symbolic antiderivative labels.
A pretrained symbolic regressor converts sampled curves into candidate expressions.
A Transformer amortizes the expensive expression recovery into direct token prediction.
Coefficient correlations and basic arithmetic combinations yield compact template rules.
A 1% curve discrepancy threshold removes many failed symbolic-regression labels.

evaluations.setting: Twenty thousand held-out functions from the same degree-limited polynomial and affine exponential/sine/cosine generators.
evaluations.result: GPT-Neo reaches 73.3%/95.7% on polynomials and 87.1%/94.8% on non-polynomials.
evaluations.baseline: Flan-T5 reaches 67.7%/85.7% and 64.6%/75.7%; the symbolic teacher reaches 65.7%/90.6% and 46.4%/71.1%.

evaluations.setting: The same direct-inference benchmark on one A6000 GPU.
evaluations.baseline: Symbolic regression after numerical quadrature takes 3.17 seconds.

evaluations.setting: 49,109 accepted polynomial and 63,409 accepted non-polynomial pseudo-labels grouped by fixed templates.
evaluations.result: The search recovers standard power, exponential, sine, and cosine rules with near-unit reported correlations.
evaluations.baseline: No alternative rule-search system or held-out operator grammar is evaluated.

limitations: Reviewer inference: only four elementary template families are covered, with bounded degree and almost no nested or composed expressions.
Reviewer inference: pseudo-label errors and rounding are evaluated against themselves rather than an exact symbolic verifier such as differentiation plus domain checks.
Reviewer inference: no template-level distribution shift tests whether the system can infer a genuinely unseen rule.
Reviewer inference: the paper's scientific-discovery framing is much broader than its supervised distillation and restricted grammar-search evidence.
Reviewer inference: model identity, data splits, decoding procedure, seeds, and uncertainty are insufficiently documented for exact reproduction.
failure_modes: Two expressions can agree on [0,4] within tolerance but differ symbolically or outside the sampled interval.
A symbolic teacher can systematically choose a misleading skeleton, which the student then learns more consistently than the truth.
Division searches become unstable when frequency coefficients approach zero, a case excluded implicitly by the generator.
Coefficient correlation can select a spurious rule when generated parameters are dependent or the grammar contains many tried hypotheses.
Expressions outside the token, operator, or skeleton vocabulary cannot be discovered regardless of numerical evidence.
reusable_insights: A numeric oracle plus symbolic compression is a useful discovery architecture, but its prior grammar and verifier must be counted as knowledge supplied to the system.
Distillation can make a slow search procedure faster and sometimes denoise its labels; it does not by itself create new knowledge.
Discovery benchmarks should hold out mechanisms or operator compositions, not merely fresh parameters from known templates.
Candidate laws should be checked by an independent exact or high-coverage verifier before being scored as discoveries.
open_questions: Can the system recover a rule for a function family whose skeleton and key operator were absent from training and search design?
How does performance change under exact derivative equivalence, out-of-interval tests, singularities, and adversarially aliasing functions?
Can grammar expansion be automated without making multiple-hypothesis false discoveries dominate?
Which minimal priors are necessary to move from numerical curves to reusable symbolic laws?
Can a closed-loop system propose and verify a genuinely new conjecture rather than reconstruct a known elementary identity?

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Learning for Symbolic Mathematics
competitive_landscape.difference: Lample and Charton train sequence models directly on generated symbolic integration and differential-equation pairs and test expression solving. This paper avoids direct antiderivative labels initially, but ultimately creates them through a pretrained symbolic regressor and trains a similar translation model.

competitive_landscape.title: End-to-end Symbolic Regression with Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Kamienny et al. predict complete expressions and constants directly from sampled values and evaluate on SRBench. The present pipeline uses that class of regressor as a pseudo-label generator, then searches integration-specific coefficient rules in a narrower domain.

competitive_landscape.title: Pretrained Language Models are Symbolic Mathematics Solvers too!
competitive_landscape.difference: Noorbakhsh et al. study sample-efficient pretrained Transformer integration and explicitly evaluate distribution shift. This paper emphasizes labels derived from numerical area and readable rule extraction but lacks the competitor's shift analysis.

competitive_landscape.title: Mathematical Discoveries from Program Search with Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: FunSearch couples an LLM with an executable evaluator and improves best-known results on an open cap-set problem and bin packing. It supplies materially stronger evidence of discovery than recovering known integration templates, though it uses pretrained human knowledge rather than trying to exclude it.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Starting from numerical area rather than antiderivative demonstrations, the pipeline learns direct integration and automatically rediscovers elementary rules.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The quadrature-to-symbolic-to-sequence pipeline and coefficient search recover accurate expressions and four standard rule families on generated data.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The numeric weak-supervision setup and explicit coefficient-rule extraction are useful packaging, but the system is not knowledge-free and the discovery claim is not established. Its function templates, symbolic regressor, algebra pretraining, operator grammar, and same-template test split make the result closer to pseudo-label distillation and constrained system identification than open scientific discovery.

reviewer_notes: Read all 22 extracted pages and visually inspected both architecture diagrams, all learning curves, latency/accuracy tables, and coefficient-correlation tables. Primary arXiv records and the Nature version of FunSearch were checked on 2026-08-23. The model-name inconsistency and discovery-scope qualifications are explicitly separated from author claims.
